verdict: the timer interrupt vector: the constants written to IE are $09, $01 and $02, never the timer bit; two writes copy a variable (probably never enabled)
GAME_SEQ case $0E of the main dispatcher: the 13 stores to GAME_SEQ ($C0A0) are the constants $01-$0D (SEQ_TITL ... SEQ_EMI), never $0E
BANK TEST: the NG branch, taken only when a bank does not hold its number at $4000 or $7FFF; every bank $01-$3F of this ROM does (a faulty ROM or mapper only)
TEST4M: the 4M OK branch, taken only when banks $20-$3F repeat $00-$1F (a 4-Mbit ROM); this ROM is 8 Mbit, bank $20 holds $20 (BGB shows 4M NG)
MK_SRAM_AGING: no pattern for R0 ($FF88); AGING starts from DATA SELECT, which copies the cursor height $35-$75 of its five rows to R0
AGE_DEC: the second byte of a pair read back wrong while the first was right: an SRAM fault only (the protected-SRAM error of BGB fails on the first byte, 00:0C30)
CHANGE_PALETTE: the return for a palette above 5; wPALETTE is 0 at boot (00:03EA) and the settings screen wraps it within 0-5 (00:144F, 00:14DD)
CHANGE_PALETTE: the return after the palette-3 swap loop, which BGB ran (00:10FA-1106, the settings screen with palette 3); the loop's counter reaches 0
TIMER_INT, the handler behind the timer vector (00:0050): see that row

Seq09_ConfigMain: the held Right / Left of the rows GAIN, OFFSET and CHG (cursor $65, $75, $85); the settings cursor moves $15, $25, $35 then jumps to $95 (PALETTE) and back (00:14F0-150B, 00:150C-1527): those rows are shown, never selected
Config_PutItem with R0 = 4 (PUT_VREF): no code of bank $00 stores 4 in R0; the edits of the unselectable rows would
Config_PutItem with R0 = 6: no code of bank $00 stores 6 in R0
Config_PutItem with R0 = 7 (PUT_OFS): the stores of 7 in R0 belong to other screens, and Config_PutItem clears R0 after each call (00:1589)
Config_PutItem with R0 = 8 (PUT_CHG_T): no code of bank $00 stores 8 in R0

PUT_OFS: the sign shown when bit 5 of the offset (wB_CNTR5) is set; the settings screen showed -1F, -0D, -0A in BGB; it needs another offset value from the sensor (a fake light in the core, 2026-11-13: MOVIE TEST with a byte plane over SRAM $A000-$AEFF, $00 / $FF / $55 / $AA and $00-$FF flips every 1 to 120 frames for 3,000 frames: not reached)
OFF_TEST: NG when a byte written with SRAM writes on does not read back (an SRAM fault only)
ON_TEST: NG when a byte written with SRAM writes off does change (a fault of the write protection only)
VB_PROTECT: the text for OK_FLAG 4, set only by the OFF_TEST NG branch (00:1AEF)
VB_PROTECT: the text for OK_FLAG 6, set only by the ON_TEST NG branch (00:1B2E); the stores to OK_FLAG are 0-6
PIC_SAVE: the return for SAVE_FLAG above 2; the stores to SAVE_FLAG are 0, 1 and 2
